chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ali from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the souls of the believers, so he said: '[They are] in chambers in Paradise, eating from its food and drinking from its drink, and they will say: Our Lord, bring upon us the Hour and fulfill for us what You promised us, and join the last of us to the first.'
ai.seo_question: Where are the souls of believers located in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* elucidates the concept of *Ruh* (soul) as a distinct entity residing in *Barzakh*, specifically in chambers within Paradise, enjoying spiritual sustenance while awaiting bodily resurrection. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the soul's experience in the grave is not merely passive but involves active supplication for the culmination of divine promise, emphasizing the unity of the community of believers across time. The supplication 'make us last and make our last join our first' underscores the desire for collective resurrection and the end of the separation caused by death.
